data.title: Neon Nights, Real Sunsets: Agoda Sees Asian Searches for Miami Stays More Than Double as the Year's Most Anticipated Video Game Launches
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Digital travel platform Agoda has recorded a 123% year-on-year increase in accommodation searches by Asian travelers for Miami on 18 November, the day before the launch of the year's most anticipated video game. Searches for the game, which is set in a fictional, Miami-inspired city, were up 96% year on year on 17–18 November. Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia showed the sharpest jumps.

After more than a decade of fan anticipation, the game drops players into a sun-soaked, neon-lit coastal city that borrows heavily from Miami's skyline, beaches and nightlife. Agoda's search data offers a snapshot of how that spotlight coincides with travel interest in the real thing, from South Beach to the wider South Florida coast.

A Region Looking Toward South Florida

Searches by Asian travelers for Miami stays between 5 and 16 November were up 18% compared to the same period in 2025. That figure climbed further on 18 November which accommodation searches on that day up 177% year on year.

South-East Asian markets led the increase. Compared with their 5–16 November daily averages, Agoda recorded on 18 November:

  • Thailand: searches for Miami stays up more than nine times
  • Vietnam: up more than seven times
  • Indonesia: up five times
  • Malaysia: up more than three times
  • South Korea: up 2.7 times
  • Taiwan: up 2.6 times
  • Japan: up more than two times

Andrew Smith, Senior Vice President, Supply, at Agoda, said: "Big cultural moments give travelers a reason to look at a destination in a new way. When a launch puts a place like Miami in front of a global audience, we see people turn that curiosity into actual searches for where they could stay. Agoda helps travelers compare accommodation across South Florida, so they can find a base that suits their plans and budget."

Where to Stay in South Florida: A Neighborhood Guide

For travelers curious about the real-life inspiration, South Florida offers a distinct experience depending on where they base themselves. Here's a closer look at four areas worth checking out.

South Beach, at the southern tip of Miami Beach, is known for its Art Deco architecture, pastel-hued buildings and Ocean Drive's neon-lit evenings. Lummus Park and the beach sit a short walk from cafes, bars and shops along Lincoln Road.

Wynwood is Miami's street-art district, where warehouse walls turn into large-scale murals. Galleries, craft breweries and food halls fill the neighborhood, which suits travelers who want a creative, walkable base.

Brickell is the city's downtown financial district, with a skyline of glass towers, rooftop lounges and waterfront dining. It offers easy access to Metromover and Brickell City Centre.

Fort Lauderdale sits about 30 miles north of Miami, with canal-lined streets, a long beachfront promenade and a boating culture that earns it the nickname "Venice of America". It offers a more relaxed pace for a longer South Florida stay.

SOURCE Agoda

data.title: Dollar Could Stay Strong in 2027 — Market Talk
data.description: The dollar is likely to remain higher for longer due to the positive implications of the AI boom, Deutsche Bank's George Saravelos says in a note. data.title: 1911 Gold Strengthens Technical Team with the Appointment of Maurice Mostert as Vice President, Technical Services
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 1911 Gold Corporation ("1911 Gold" or the "Company") () (OTCQX: AUMBF) (FRA: 2KY) is pleased to announce the appointment of Maurice Mostert, P.Eng., a well-regarded and seasoned mining engineer as Vice President, Technical Services, effective November 18, 2026. Mr. Mostert will lead the technical services function as it advances the 100%-owned, built, and fully permitted, True North Gold Project ("True North"), located in southeastern Manitoba, Canada.

Mr. Mostert will lead the technical strategy including mine design, mine planning and scheduling, and will oversee future technical studies as 1911 Gold advances True North towards a decision to restart operations and production in 2027.

Shaun Heinrichs, President and CEO, stated, "I am extremely pleased to welcome Maurice, a well-respected and  highly experienced mine engineer to the team. Maurice brings extensive knowledge and hands on recent, directly relevant experience leading the technical services function through the restart of an unground gold mine in Canada. His depth in underground mine planning and study management strengthens our technical team as we continue on the path of development to support making a decision on a full mine restart and production next year."

Maurice Mostert, P.Eng., Vice President, Technical Services

Mr. Mostert is a mining engineer with more than 30 years of experience in underground and open pit mining across operations, mine planning, technical studies and consulting in Canada, the United States, South America and Africa. He most recently served as Vice President, Technical Services at West Red Lake Gold Mines Ltd. (2023 to 2025), where he built the technical services team and led the technical work supporting the restart of the Madsen Mine in Red Lake, Ontario, including management of the project's Pre-Feasibility Study.

Previously, Mr. Mostert was Manager, Western Canada at Mining Plus Canada, where he managed feasibility-level and optimization studies for mining projects in Canada, the United States and South America. His earlier career includes senior mine planning and study roles with SRK Consulting in Johannesburg and with Gold Fields at the South Deep mine in South Africa.

Mr. Mostert holds a Master of Science in Engineering (Mining Engineering) from the University of the Witwatersrand and a Bachelor of Business Administration from the University of South Africa. He is a Professional Engineer registered with Engineers and Geoscientists British Columbia, a Fellow of the Southern African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, and a member of the Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum.

Mr. Mostert is Managing Director and Principal Engineer of Verum Mining Consultants Ltd. ("Verum"), and his services as Vice President, Technical Services are provided to the Company under a consulting services agreement between 1911 Gold and Verum, whereby the Company will pay a monthly consulting fee of $35,000, with the initial term expiring on December 31, 2027 . The Company has also granted Mr. Mostert, 350,000 stock options to purchase common shares of the Company, pursuant to the Company's Long-Term Incentive Plan. Such options have an exercise price $0.52 per share and expire November 18, 2031. The Options will vest as to one-third immediately and one-third after the first and second anniversaries of the date of grant. The granting of the options is subject to policies by the TSX Venture Exchange.

About 1911 Gold Corporation1911 Gold is an advanced gold explorer and developer focused on its 100%-owned True North Gold Project in the Archean Rice Lake Greenstone Belt in Manitoba, Canada. The Company controls a large ~62,000-hectare land package with numerous past-producing gold operations within trucking distance of the fully built and permitted True North mine and mill complex. 1911 Gold is positioning itself to make a decision on restarting operations in the future, highlighting a unique investment opportunity with significant exploration upside. The strategy is to build a district-scale gold mining operation around centralized and expandable infrastructure to support a socially and environmentally responsible, long-term mining operation with a growing mineral resource base.

1911 Gold's True North complex and exploration land package are located in an area of importance to Indigenous Nations, communities, and rights-holders. 1911 Gold looks forward to maintaining open, cooperative, respectful, and meaningful communication while also engaging with other stakeholders, to foster mutually beneficial working relationships.

ON BEHALF OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS

Shaun Heinrichs, President and CEO

www.1911Gold.com

data.title: Asian gasoline margin plunges to over three-year lows on ample supplies
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Asian gasoline margins plummeted around 69% this week as abundant supplies from China and the Middle East weighed on crack spreads, traders and analysts said on Thursday.

The refining profit, or crack, (GL92-SIN-CRK) for gasoline shrank to $2.67 per barrel over Brent crude, the lowest level since October 2023, from a record peak of $50.53 on October 1.

"Increased Chinese exports are further weighing on the sentiment," Stuti Jhunjhunwala, oil market analyst at Energy Aspects, said.

Gasoline crack spreads usually shrink heading into the northern hemisphere's winter, when fuel demand falls, however, this year they hit record highs on a tight supply outlook, caused by the Middle East war, Russia's export ban and lower inventories at key trading hubs.

The margins fell to six-month lows at the end of October and have been on a downward trend since amid hopes of higher supplies.

"Plenty of supplies from China and year-end destocking causing the fall," a Dubai-based light distillate trader said.

Meanwhile, gasoline imports at the Singapore trading and blending hub tanked 69% to 67,000 tons (about 566,000 barrels) in the week to November 18, while exports rose about 13% on-week to roughly 459,000 tons, government data showed.

The top supplier was China at about 50,000 tons, while the top destination for exports was Australia at 111,000 tons.

data.title: FTSE 100 Hovers Near 6-Week Lows On Consumer Sector Decline
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Despite a good show by other major European markets thanks to Anthropic's record IPO offering, U.K.'s equity benchmark FTSE 100 dropped to a near 6-week low Thursday morning, weighed down by losses in the consumer sector. The moves were mostly stock specific with investors reacting to a slew of earnings announcements.

The FTSE 100, which advanced to 10,569.50 earlier in the session, dropped to 10,519.18 and was down 26.57 points or 0.25% at 10,524.60 nearly half an hour before noon.

Investec tumbled 6.6% after reporting weaker momentum in its U.K. operations. JD Sports Fashion dropped about 4.2% after lowering the top end of its annual profit guidance.

Vodafone Group, National Grid, Imperial Brands, Severn Trent, Reckitt Benckiser, Unilever, 3i Group and Coca-Cola Europacific Partners lost 2%-3%.

British American Tobacco, United Utilities, Experian, Convatec Group, British Land Company, Admiral Group, Tesco, GSK, Diageo and Associated British Foods were among the other notable losers.

Mulberry Group shares tanked 22%. The luxury leather goods group reported a loss before tax for the 26 weeks ended 26 September 2026 of £33.4m despite making strong progress in its turnaround.

Babcock International soared 8% after the defense engineering and nuclear services group reported a 13% rise in first half underlying operating profit, and raised its full-year guidance.

Halma moved up 3.7% after the safety and technology group reported that its first-half bottom line totaled GBP219.9 million, or GBP0.5802 per share. This compares with GBP186.8 million, or GBP0.4929 per share, last year.

Miners Anglo American Plc and Antofagasta climbed 2.7% and 2.3%, respectively. Glencore gained 1.7% and Fresnillo moved up 1.5%

Polar Capital Technology Trust Holdings gained 3.5% and Burberry Group moved up 3.2%. Computacenter, Pershing Square Holdings, IMI, Rolls-Royce Holdings and Smiths Group gained 2%-3%.

Johnson Matthey gained more than 2%. The specialty chemicals group upgraded its full-year profit guidance after delivering a robust set of half-year results. Melrose Industries, Barclays, Airtel Africa, Games Workshop and Spirax Group also moved notably higher.

In economic news, the Industrial Trends Survey dat from the Confederation of British Industry showed UK manufacturing orders improved notably in November.

The order book balance rose to -12% in November from -32% in October. Export orders also strengthened in November, with the balance rising to -19% from -25%.

In the three months to November, output volumes expanded for the first time since May 2024. The indicator posted +9 percent compared to -10% in the quarter to October.
